cards.text: Paul is being held, and the Jews have accused him. The commander wants to learn the real reason, so the next day he orders the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble. That's not a meeting, friend, that's the WHOLE group chat showing up in person.

cards.question: For the meeting, the commander keeps Paul locked up and has the Sanhedrin come to him.

cards.text: The commander releases Paul, brings him down and has him stand before them. Paul looks directly at the Sanhedrin, and there's no small talk and no warm-up.

cards.question: Paul opens by telling the Sanhedrin how he has conducted himself before God. How does he say he has lived?

answers.text: In all good conscience to this day
In fear and trembling every day
With many regrets to this day

cards.text: Paul gets ONE sentence out. Then comes an order for the men standing near him to strike him on the mouth.

cards.question: The ___ Ananias orders the men near Paul to strike him on the mouth.

cards.text: Paul fires right back: "God will strike you, you whitewashed wall!" Friend, I've been called crumbly, dusty and blurry, but never a WHITEWASHED WALL.

cards.question: Paul says the man who gave the order sits there to judge him by the law. How does Paul say that man breaks the law himself?

answers.text: By ordering that Paul be struck
By judging Paul on the Sabbath
By taking money from the crowd

cards.text: Those standing nearby say, "How dare you insult the high priest of God!" Uh-oh.

cards.question: Paul says that when he called the man a whitewashed wall, he knew the man was the high priest.
Paul calls them brothers and quotes Scripture right away. What does that Scripture say not to do?

answers.text: Speak evil about the ruler of your people
Bring your brother before the judges
Turn away from the elders of your people

cards.text: Paul knows some of the Sanhedrin are Sadducees and the others Pharisees. So he calls out, "Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee."

cards.question: Paul tells the Sanhedrin he is on trial because of his hope in the ___ of the dead.

cards.text: As soon as he says it, a dispute breaks out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly is divided. Paul just walked into the break room and asked who changed the thermostat.

cards.question: Why does Paul's line about the resurrection divide the Pharisees and the Sadducees?

answers.text: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection
The Pharisees say Paul has left the law
The Sadducees say Paul is no Pharisee

cards.question: The Pharisees acknowledge the resurrection, angels and spirits.

cards.text: A great clamor rises, and some scribes from the party of the Pharisees get up and argue sharply. The dead batteries I shared that drawer with used to fight over who had the most charge left, and even THEY never got this loud.

cards.question: The scribes from the party of the Pharisees demand that Paul be punished.

cards.text: Nope. They say, "We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?"

cards.question: The dispute grows so violent that the commander is afraid they will tear Paul to pieces. What does he order?

answers.text: Soldiers take Paul by force to the barracks
Soldiers march the whole council outside
Soldiers flog Paul until he tells the truth

cards.text: The following night, the Lord stands near Paul and says, "Take courage!" Friend, I spent years in the back of a dark junk drawer, and two words like that at night are better than a fresh batch straight out of the oven.

cards.question: The Lord tells Paul that as he has testified about Him in Jerusalem, he must also testify in ___.

cards.text: Rome, friend, ROME! We're pausing the oven right here, but Paul's story still has plenty of pages left.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Paul knows the two parties and identifies himself as a Pharisee. It gives no information from which the baker can infer resurrection rather than judgment or memory, so the blank asks for the next, as-yet-unheard wording by luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: 'Nope.' plus the two sentences in the scribes' quotation. That exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The preceding story card supplies only 'Take courage!' and no earlier card points toward Rome rather than Antioch or Damascus. The baker cannot reason out this destination and can only guess the unseen word.
